newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ulster Bank, NIB to develop Mondex in Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Ulster Bank, NIB to develop Mondex in Ireland.

text.p: National Irish Bank, the Irish arm of National Australia Bank, and Ulster Bank said on Tuesday that they had purchased the Irish franchise for Mondex and would form a joint venture company to exploit the franchise.
Mondex is a new payment smartcard being introduced by leading banks and retailers world-wide which brings together the advantages of paying by cash and the convenience of paying by card.
Work has already commenced on the development of the supporting infrastructure and implementation plans and the two banks expect to launch pilots in 1998, a statement said.

"The next step for the two banks will be to define/finalise the form of their joint venture and to establish how best to take Mondex forward to the benefit of Irish consumers, retailers and the financial community."
Philip Halpin, chief operating officer at NIB, said the joint venture gave the bank the opportunity to bring the benefits of international payments technology to the Republic of Ireland.
"We will be capitalising on the significant investment in Mondex made by our parent company, National Australia Bank, in the Australasian region and the in U.S. during 1996," he said.

Ulster Bank, a unit of National Westminster Bank Plc, said Mondex would assist it in providing all its customers with cost efficient methods of obtaining financial information and making and receiving payments.
